INFR11269 Coursework: individual - review marking 
rubric 
The individual review is marked out of 100 and contributes   30%   of your coursework mark. It assesses 
your ability to understand, evaluate and help improve another group's work. It does not affect that 
group's mark. 
Criteria 
Criterion   Marks   What is assessed   Boundary 
Accurate 
understanding   20 
A faithful account of the question, 
approach, contribution and findings; correct 
representation of the authors' claims 
throughout the review 
What the reviewed work 
actually says and does 
Evidence - based 
evaluation   50 
Specific, technically reasoned strengths 
and weaknesses; relevant supporting 
references; proportionate judgements that 
distinguish errors, uncertainties and 
limitations 
Whether the evaluative 
judgements are justified 
Constructive detailed 
comments   30 
Prioritised, feasible suggestions and useful 
clarification questions; an explanation of 
how they would improve the work; clear 
and respectful communication 
How effectively the review 
helps the authors improve 
or clarify the work 
Total   100 
Complete the four required fields and include at least three distinct strengths and three distinct 
weaknesses. More comments do not automatically earn more marks. Marks depend on accuracy, 
reasoning and usefulness, not on how positive or negative the review is. 
Performance descriptions 
The ranges describe performance within each criterion. For example, performance assessed at 70% 
in a 50 - mark criterion receives 35 marks. 
Accurate understanding 
Performance level   Description 
Excellent: 70 – 100% 
Demonstrates precise, integrated understanding of the question, technical approach 
and findings. Accurately distinguishes the supplied baseline, the authors' contribution, 
stated claims and qualifications, preserving these distinctions throughout. Selects the 
essential details without distorting the work or importing unsupported assumptions. 
Good: 60 – 69% 
Accurately explains the question, contribution, approach and principal findings, and 
preserves the important qualifications. Shows clear understanding of how these 
elements connect; minor omissions or imprecision do not materially change the 
account. 
Satisfactory: 50 – 
59% 
Correctly summarises the main question, approach and findings and identifies the 
authors' contribution. The account is largely descriptive, with limited integration of the 
technical details and some loss of nuance, but no fundamental misunderstanding. 
Limited: 40 – 49% 
Recognises the broad purpose and outcome, but important details, distinctions or 
qualifications are missing or confused. Understanding is uneven, and parts of the 
review rely on assumptions rather than a faithful account of the submission.

2 
Performance level   Description 
Inadequate: 0 – 39% 
Does not establish a reliable understanding of the work. Substantial 
misrepresentation, major omissions or unsupported assumptions obscure the 
question, contribution or findings and undermine the review. 
Evidence - based evaluation 
Performance level   Description 
Excellent: 70 – 100% 
Selects the strengths and weaknesses most consequential to the investigation and 
substantiates them with precise evidence and rigorous technical reasoning. Explains 
how each affects the credibility or significance of specific claims, weighs 
counterevidence and uncertainty where relevant, and makes proportionate 
judgements without generic or speculative criticism. 
Good: 60 – 69% 
Provides distinct, specific strengths and weaknesses supported by relevant evidence 
and sound technical reasoning. Explains their importance to the main claims and 
distinguishes errors from limitations. Some judgements lack the depth, prioritisation or 
qualification needed for an outstanding evaluation. 
Satisfactory: 50 – 
59% 
Identifies relevant strengths and weaknesses, supports the main observations with 
evidence and gives reasonable explanations of their importance. Evaluation is 
competent but uneven: several points remain surface - level, loosely prioritised or 
insufficiently qualified. 
Limited: 40 – 49% 
Offers some valid observations, but much of the evaluation is descriptive, generic or 
weakly supported. Reasoning does not consistently establish why points matter, and 
repetition, unsupported assumptions or disproportionate criticism reduce its 
usefulness. 
Inadequate: 0 – 39% 
Provides insufficient defensible evaluation. Strengths or weaknesses are largely 
unsubstantiated, materially incorrect or disconnected from the work, with little 
explanation of their significance for the authors' claims. 
Constructive detailed comments 
Performance level   Description 
Excellent: 70 – 100% 
Develops a focused, prioritised set of improvements tailored to the work and feasible 
within its scope. Specifies what to change or test, why it matters, and how the 
resulting evidence would resolve uncertainty or strengthen the argument. Anticipates 
relevant trade - offs and communicates precise, respectful guidance. 
Good: 60 – 69% 
Offers specific, feasible suggestions or clarification questions addressing the 
important issues. Explains the intended benefit and gives enough detail for the 
authors to act. Prioritisation is sensible, although expected outcomes or practical 
trade - offs are not fully developed. 
Satisfactory: 50 – 
59% 
Provides relevant, actionable suggestions and explains their general purpose. Some 
recommendations are useful, but priorities, implementation details or the evidence 
needed to judge their benefit remain underdeveloped. 
Limited: 40 – 49% 
Makes some potentially helpful suggestions, but advice is broad, repetitive or only 
loosely connected to the diagnosed issues. The authors would need substantial 
interpretation to decide what to do and what improvement to expect. 
Inadequate: 0 – 39% 
Provides little actionable assistance. Recommendations are absent, largely generic, 
impractical or disconnected from the work, and do not explain how the authors could 
improve or clarify the submission.
